solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ancient spoils put back in compartment in state of abeyance

indicators.note: the old and turned-back pieces sit inside the compartment word

parts.note: a cage is an enclosed compartment
ancient means old

indicators.note: put back means the word for spoils is read from right to left

parts.note: spoils, as food does, means rots

explanation.surface: Old loot is returned to a storage locker, left there indefinitely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoils' looks like plunder but is the verb, as food goes off; 'put back' turns that word round before it joins the old piece inside the compartment.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans kept in cold storage are shelved, held over in suspension for later.

clue.text: Something maybe in ring, with love offered to mate

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scores, the letter O
a mate is a pal, a friend

explanation.surface: A ring given with love to a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is a gemstone, the kind of stone often set in a ring.

clue.text: Tree disease Richard spotted around Lincoln, going north

indicators.note: spotted around says the name for Richard is placed round the other piece

parts.note: Dick is a short form of Richard

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means the name is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln's familiar name

explanation.surface: Someone named Richard saw a tree blight near Lincoln on the way north.
explanation.walkthrough: Spotted dick is a British suet pudding, which makes 'Richard spotted' look like one phrase; 'going north' turns the president's name upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieback is a disease in which trees or shrubs die progressively from the shoot tips inward.

clue.text: Old rocker — one to be locked up, restrained

indicators.note: to be locked up says the numeral goes inside the rocker word

parts.note: a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British rock-and-roll youth
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An aged rock fan needs to be jailed and held back.
explanation.walkthrough: A rocker here is a Teddy boy, a 1950s British youth subculture, not a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Tied and restrained both mean bound so as not to move freely.

clue.text: Sympathy established in chat over drink

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the chat word sits above the drink word

parts.note: rap is slang for talk or chat
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Friendly understanding grows while talking over a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapport is a sympathetic, harmonious relationship between people.

clue.text: Female to dress up — lad taking no notice!

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the dress word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to rig out is to dress

indicators.note: taking no notice says the notice word is dropped from lad

parts.note: taken as written before removal
an ad is a notice, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A woman dresses up while a boy pays her no attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RIG into GIR; 'taking no' removes AD from LAD, leaving L.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl is a young female person, so the noun fits the adjective-looking clue word used as a noun.

clue.text: Pub snack — sounds unpleasant?

definitions.meaning: pork ... are crisp fried pork rind eaten with beer in British pubs
scratching noises, like nails on a board, are grating to hear

explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a fried pork-rind bar nibble and the grating noises of scraping.

clue.text: Country workers — courageous folk on field wearing gloves?

parts.note: game means plucky, willing
wicket-keepers and goalkeepers wear gloves on the field of play

explanation.surface: Rural labourers are brave sorts who play in gloves.
explanation.walkthrough: Wicketkeepers in cricket and goalkeepers in football are the gloved players.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamekeepers are employed on rural estates to rear and protect game birds.

clue.text: Sad Aussie who may work in the churchyard?

definitions.text: who may work in the churchyard?

parts.note: grave means serious, solemn
digger is a slang name for an Australian, especially a soldier

explanation.surface: A gloomy Australian might find a job in a cemetery.
explanation.definitionFit: A gravedigger prepares burial plots, often in the yard around a church.

clue.text: People in administration uncommunicative, with air getting tense

parts.note: secret here means secretive, giving nothing away
an aria is an operatic air, a tune
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Officials are tight-lipped as the atmosphere grows strained.
explanation.definitionFit: A secretariat is the administrative office and staff of an organisation.

clue.text: The chocs a ma chewed — possible cause of this?

definitions.text: The chocs a ma chewed — possible cause of this?

indicators.note: chewed means the preceding words are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Mum munched the chocolates and now wonders what is causing her pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chewed' rearranges THECHOCSAMA; the whole clue then describes eating sweets that bring on the very complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorging on chocolates is a plausible cause of an aching belly.

clue.text: Eddy left trailing behind dog

indicators.note: trailing behind puts the left abbreviation after the dog word

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A whirl of water with the dog lagging behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A curl of water or smoke is a spiralling eddy.

clue.text: Water course burst finally on to meadow

indicators.note: on to places the final letter after the meadow word

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of burst

explanation.surface: A stream bursts its banks onto a field.
explanation.definitionFit: A leat is an open channel carrying water, typically to a mill.

clue.text: A social event collects very little money up front

indicators.note: collects means the dance word gathers the short letter inside it

parts.note: a dance is a social event
V is a short abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A party raises a tiny sum in prepayment.
explanation.definitionFit: An advance is money paid before it is due, such as a loan against wages.

clue.text: Irish town producing top female athlete (as she was)

definitions.meaning: The county town of County Clare in Ireland
Jessica ..., Olympic heptathlon champion in 2012, now competes under her married name ...-Hill

explanation.definitionFit: Both the Clare town and the British heptathlete's maiden surname share this name.

clue.text: Coarse stuff made with alcoholic drink and butter

parts.note: grog is rum diluted with water, or any drink
a ram butts with its head, so it is a butter

explanation.surface: Something rough made from booze and dairy spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the dairy spread but one who butts.
explanation.definitionFit: Grogram is a coarse fabric of silk mixed with mohair or wool.

clue.text: Mucky stuff in weapon little good — remove ultimately

parts.note: a gun is a weapon
G is a short form of good

indicators.note: ultimately selects the last letter of remove

explanation.surface: Filth inside a gun — a little good clean will shift it eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunge is British slang for sticky, unpleasant gunk.

clue.text: Instrument of torture, nothing audible

indicators.note: audible says the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: nowt is northern English dialect for nothing

explanation.surface: A torture device that makes no sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A knout was a Russian whip used for flogging criminals.

clue.text: A sort of ending? Bring back a medical practitioner

indicators.note: bring back means the words that follow are read in reverse

parts.note: doc is short for doctor

explanation.surface: Is it the end when you recall a doctor?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring back' turns ADOC around as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is a concluding passage, especially of a piece of music.

clue.text: Notice bits being nibbled from sides of the ear

indicators.note: nibbling the edges strips the first and last letters off notice

explanation.surface: Someone notices pieces chewed off the edges of an ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic is the medical adjective relating to ears.

clue.text: One having no pounds to burn

indicators.note: having no means the pounds letter is removed

parts.note: single means one
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from libra

explanation.surface: Someone broke with money to burn.
explanation.definitionFit: To singe is to burn slightly on the surface.

clue.text: Bread snatched around end of meal

indicators.note: around says the stolen word goes round the single letter

parts.note: snatched means stolen

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of meal

explanation.surface: A loaf grabbed at the close of dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Stollen is a German fruit loaf, a sweet bread eaten at Christmas.

clue.text: Times to ponder cut short for old scholar

parts.note: eras are periods, times

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of the ponder word is removed

parts.note: to muse is to ponder

explanation.surface: Time to reflect, cut short, for a learned man of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus was a Dutch Renaissance humanist scholar.

clue.text: Takes in various gents — is offering accommodation

indicators.note: is offering accommodation means is houses the other letters
various means the letters of gents appear in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A host takes in a mix of men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gents' looks like the men themselves, but 'various' only jumbles its letters, which the two-letter word then houses.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest is to take food or drink into the body.

clue.text: Country with a form of technology brought by engineers in time

indicators.note: in places the technology and engineers letters inside the time word

parts.note: an era is a period of time
IT is information technology
RE stands for Royal Engineers, the British Army corps

explanation.surface: A nation where engineers introduce a technology over time.
explanation.definitionFit: Eritrea is a nation in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Former England cricket captain losing wicket, energetic type

indicators.note: losing means the wicket letter is taken away

parts.note: David Gower captained England at cricket in the 1980s
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: An ex-England skipper loses his wicket but is a lively sort.
explanation.walkthrough: David Gower was an elegant England batsman and captain; cricket is England's summer bat-and-ball game.
explanation.definitionFit: A goer is a lively, active person or thing.

clue.text: Raw duck? Cook again

parts.note: raw skin is red and sore
a duck is a score of zero in cricket, the letter O

explanation.surface: This bird's undercooked; put it back on.
explanation.definitionFit: To redo is to do something again, here to prepare food once more.

clue.text: Ones put in place subsequently

indicators.note: put in signals the letters are tucked within the following words

explanation.surface: Things placed later on.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace is the one in a pack of cards, so aces are ones.

clue.text: Reluctant to ignore learner's solemn appeal

indicators.note: to ignore means the learner letter is left out

parts.note: loath means reluctant
L is the learner driver's plate letter

explanation.surface: Unwilling to disregard a novice's earnest plea.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath is a solemn promise often calling on God as witness.

clue.text: Nob may get bowled out at any time

indicators.note: out says the bowled letter is removed from the head word

parts.note: nob and bonce are both British slang for the head
B is the cricket abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: A toff might be bowled out whenever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nob' looks like a posh person but here means head.
explanation.definitionFit: Once can mean ever, at any time, as in 'if once you start'.

clue.text: New paler glue serves as substitute

indicators.note: new means the letters of paler come out freshly arranged

parts.note: cement is an adhesive, a glue

explanation.surface: A fresh, lighter adhesive is used instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A replacement takes the place of another, as a substitute does.

clue.text: Awful dusty mess on electronic equipment?

indicators.note: awful means the following letters are in a terrible state, jumbled

explanation.surface: A dreadful dusty clutter piled on the electronics.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound system is electronic equipment for playing amplified audio.
